evidence.says: Script Extender declares eoc::LootingStateComponent::Looter_M at +0x0 (Script Extender's header BG3Extender/GameDefinitions/Components/Data.h calls it Looter_M; offset computed from the header)
Script Extender declares eoc::LootingStateComponent::State at +0x8 (Script Extender's header BG3Extender/GameDefinitions/Components/Data.h calls it State; offset computed from the header)

Windows save of the component, bg3_dx11.exe+0x25A4F90 (the model loader bg3.exe+0x25A51F0 is inside it): for each component it writes the 16-byte model entry {EntityId from +0, byte +8, dword +0xC} - so the dword is at +0xC, inside the 16-byte registry size. Script Extender declares it `int field_24` after `uint8_t State` (Data.h:239), which also puts it at +0xC; field_24 is a machine name for an offset it does not have, so the field is called field_C here (legacy field_24). The game's own name is not known.

survey.names: Every name here is Script Extender's author's (his headers), not the game's own: they are kept because they are what the extender's Lua answers to and what bg3_verify compares, and every field carries the rung `unknown` because no rung of section 7 is that - not game (no FieldMeta or macOS name behind it), not toolkit, not inferred (ours, with evidence in the record). A name is raised from `unknown` only with evidence, by `gatekit names set`.
